plain.text: Judah left his brothers and married a Canaanite woman. They had three sons, Er, Onan and Shelah. Judah got a wife named Tamar for Er, but Er was wicked in the LORD's sight and died. By custom, the next brother was to have children with the widow to continue his brother's line, but Onan refused to give his brother an heir, and he also died. Judah told Tamar to wait until Shelah grew up, but then did not give her to him. Later, Tamar disguised herself and sat by the road. Judah, thinking she was a prostitute, slept with her and left his seal, cord and staff as a pledge. When Tamar was found to be pregnant, Judah ordered her to be burned. She sent him his own seal, cord and staff: "I am pregnant by the man who owns these." Judah recognised them and said, "She is more righteous than I, since I wouldn't give her to my son Shelah."

Tamar gave birth to twins. During the birth one put out his hand, and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on it, but his brother came out first. He was named Perez, and the one with the thread was Zerah. (Perez became an ancestor of King David.)

summary.bigIdea: Judah's failures are exposed, and he admits that Tamar was more righteous than he was.
points: Judah fails to keep his promise to his widowed daughter-in-law Tamar.
Tamar takes a bold step to secure her rights.
Judah confesses, "She is more righteous than I." Her son Perez becomes an ancestor of David.
summary.reflection: Judah finally admitted he was wrong. What makes admitting we're wrong so hard, and so important?
